chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Amra al-Sulami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked him, and said: 'I used to go frequently on military expeditions, travel far in seeking reward, and prolong my absences. Then that was prohibited for me, and they said: There is no military expedition except with a just Imam. So what is your view — may God keep you well?'

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If you wish, I can give you a general answer, and if you wish, I can give you a specific one.' He said: 'Rather, give me a general answer.' He said: 'Indeed, God — Mighty and Majestic — will resurrect people according to their intentions on the Day of Resurrection.'

He (the narrator) said: It was as if he desired the specific answer. He said: 'Then give me a specific one — may God keep you well.' So he said: 'Give me a case.' The man said: 'I went on a military expedition and encountered the polytheists — is it befitting to fight them before inviting them (to Islam)?' He said: 'If they had attacked and been fought and fought back, then you may proceed on that basis. But if they were a people who had not attacked and had not fought, then it is not permissible for you to fight them until you invite them.'

The man said: 'So I invited them, and one responded to me, affirming Islam in his heart, and he was within Islam. But injustice was then done against him in judgment, his sanctity was violated, his wealth was taken, and transgression was committed against him — so how does this matter turn out, since I was the one who invited him?' He said: 'Both of you will be rewarded for what occurred. And him being with you — protecting your sanctity from behind, defending your qibla, safeguarding your Book, and preserving your blood — is better than him being against you, demolishing your qibla, violating your sanctity, shedding your blood, and burning your Book.'

key_terms.إمام عادل: Just Imam — a technical term in Shia jurisprudence referring specifically to the infallible Imam or his authorized deputy
key_terms.الحرمة: Sanctity, inviolability (hurma); the protected status of a Muslim's person, honor, and property
key_terms.الغزو: Military expedition, armed raid (ghazw); in Shia fiqh, offensive jihad is conditional on the presence of a just Imam
key_terms.القبلة: Qibla — the direction of prayer toward Mecca; here used as a symbol of Islamic identity and religious practice
key_terms.النيات: Intentions (niyyat); the foundational principle that deeds are judged by their underlying intentions

ai.seo_question: Is military jihad permissible without a just Imam in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith records a detailed jurisprudential dialogue between a man and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) concerning military expeditions (jihad) conducted without a just Imam. The Imam first offers the concise universal principle that God judges people by their intentions, then proceeds to clarify specific rulings: fighting is only permissible against those who have already attacked, and only after inviting non-combatants to Islam. When asked about the moral responsibility for a convert who suffers injustice, the Imam reassures both parties that they will be rewarded, and argues that having this convert as an ally who defends Islamic institutions is better than having him as an enemy who would destroy them. This hadith reflects the early Shi'i jurisprudential position that offensive jihad is suspended during the occultation of the just Imam.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Amara Al Salmy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘A man asked him<sup>asws</sup>, so he said, ‘I used to be frequent in the military expeditions, and go far in seeking the Recompense, and long absences, so that was prohibited unto me, and they (people) said, ‘Do not go on military expeditions except with a Just Imam<sup>asws</sup>. So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view, may Allah<sup>saww</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well?.’

So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you so desire, that I<sup>asws</sup> should generalise it for you, I<sup>asws</sup> will generalise, and if you so desire to I<sup>asws</sup> particularise it for you, I<sup>asws</sup> will particularise’. So he said, ‘But, generalise’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Resurrect the people upon their intentions, on the Day of Judgement’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So it was as if he<sup>asws</sup> wanted to summarise it for him’.

He said, ‘So particularise it for me, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give me<sup>asws</sup> (a particular instance)’. So the man said, ‘I go on a military expedition and I come across the Polytheists, so is it befitting for me to fight them before I invite them (to Al-Islam)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If they had attacked you and fought and killed, so you go by that, and if they were a people who did not attack and did not kill, so there is no leeway for you to fight them until you invite them’.

The man said, ‘Supposing I invite them, and one of them responds to me with a (positive) answer and agrees with Al-Islam in his heart, and injustice was done upon him in the decision, and his sactitiy was violated, and his wealth was taken, and he was transgressed upon, so how would it be with the going out (for Jihad), and I had invited him?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Both of you would be Recompensed upon whatever was from that, and he was with you protecting your sanctity behind you, and defending your Qiblah, and safeguarding your Book, and saving your blood. This is better than if he happened to be against you demolishing your Qiblah, and violating your sanctity, and shedding your blood, and burning your Book’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu ‘Amrah al-Sullamiy who has said the following:

“A man once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I would mobilize (against the enemy) very often, stay away from asking for compensation and remain absent for a long time. This was called impermissible for me and they said, ‘There is no mobilization (against the enemy) without the Imam of justice.’ May Allah keep you well, what do you say about it?’

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, said, ‘I can say it for you in general terms and if you want I can say it to you in clear terms.’ The man said, ‘Say it in general terms.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, will resurrect people on the Day of Judgment according to their intentions.’

The narrator has said that it seemed as if he wanted the Imam to say it in clear terms. He said, ‘Make it for me in clear terms, may Allah keep you well.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Explain it.’ The man said, ‘I mobilized and faced the pagans. Should I fight them before calling them to Allah?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If they mobilize and fight, you are drawn in it. If they are a people who have not mobilized and had not fought, you can do nothing but to call them to Allah.’

The man said, ‘I called them to Allah. One of them accepted the call, affirmed al-Islam in his heart and lived as a Muslim but injustice was done to him in judgment, his honor was violated, his property taken and he was subjected to transgression. What is the solution when I was the one to call him to Allah?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Both of you deserve rewards in the matter. He is with you to shield your honor, protect your Qiblah (the sacred location), to defend your book and save your life. This is better for you than his being against you, destroy your Qiblah, violate your honor, shed your blood and burn your book.’”
